ecorp-netops: Hey @redwood team — since ~04:10 UTC our apps started getting `ERR_TLS_HANDSHAKE` talking to the Private control plane. Happens from our prod VPC only, dev VPC is fine. Any quick checks?

Anna - Support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact error and a small tcpdump/openssl snippet? Also which control-plane endpoint (region) are you hitting?

ecrop-netops: Hitting `private-controlplane.us-west-2.redwood.example` (customer VPC peering + egress NAT). Error from our side: `tlsv1 alert unknown ca` in logs, but on packet captures I see a bunch of `RST` after ClientHello.

Michael - EngOncall: Can you share `openssl s_client -connect private-controlplane.us-west-2.redwood.example:443 -tls1_3 -msg -debug` output (sanitized)? That'll show the ClientHello and server response.

ecrop-netops: Pasting minimal sanitized output:```
$ openssl s_client -connect private-controlplane.us-west-2.redwood.example:443 -tls1_3 -msg -debug
CONNECTED(00000005)
>>> TLS 1.3, ClientHello
...
<<< TLS 1.3, Alert, description = unexpected_message
139711234567808:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:s3_pkt.c:1493:SSL alert number 48
```

Jia - Eng-Infra: The `unexpected_message` + `unknown ca` combo suggests an inline device is terminating or rewriting TLS. Does your egress NGFW perform SSL inspection or TLS proxying?

ecrop-netops: Yes we have an NGFW (CorpProxy) doing TLS inspection for outbound. We thought the control plane mTLS would be allowed via our egress allowlist by IP, but maybe it still intercepts.

Lena - Security: For Private control plane, we require mutual TLS — the client presents its certificate and we validate CN/fingerprint. If the NGFW terminates TLS and re-issues its own cert, the control plane will see a different certificate chain and fail. Did you configure passthrough for that destination?

ecrop-netops: We added IPs to the allowlist but we didn't set TLS bypass/passthrough; just allowed outbound TCP/443 to the control-plane IPs.

Anna - Support: That matches common failures. Two quick repro suggestions: 1) From a host inside your prod VPC, run `curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://private-controlplane...` to see if mutual TLS negotiation completes. 2) If you can tcpdump, check for `RST` coming from the NGFW appliance IP right after ClientHello.

ecrop-netops: Ran the `curl` with our client cert: `curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca`. tcpdump shows: `ClientHello -> NGFW -> RST from NGFW -> Client`. No ServerHello seen.

Michael - EngOncall: Interesting. Another angle: some TLS proxies rewrite SNI or strip ALPN which confuses the server side and can trigger a reset if the control plane expects a specific SNI for routing to mTLS-enabled backend. Can you confirm SNI in the ClientHello and whether the proxy rewrites it?

ecrop-netops: We captured ClientHello; SNI is `private-controlplane.us-west-2.redwood.example`. The NGFW claim is it preserves SNI but rewrites the certificate chain.

Jia - Eng-Infra: Two important checks on our side: 1) Are you NATing traffic such that source IPs appear as a corporate egress IP? If so, we need that IP in our allowlist and we should validate the cert chain doesn't get replaced. 2) Can you share the client cert chain fingerprint (sha256) so we can correlate logs on the control plane? (You can DM us the fingerprint)

ecrop-netops: Source egress IP: 52.9.33.120. We DM'ed the client cert SHA256: `3a:9b:...:f2`.

deploy-bot: [deploy] controlplane/us-west-2: new rollouts paused due to external auth errors (alert id: cp-2026-042).

Lena - Security: @Jia @Michael we should check if the control plane is rejecting connections because the cert chain presented to it is missing the customer client cert. If the NGFW is terminating mTLS and re-issuing, the server will see NGFW's cert and not perform client auth. That would cause handshake failure with `unknown ca` on the client because server's cert won't chain to the expected CA.

Michael - EngOncall: Agreed. Also ask customer: does the NGFW perform TLS introspection using a private CA (i.e., it issues its own leaf cert signed by corp-root)? If yes, passthrough is required for mutual TLS endpoints.

ecrop-netops: Confirmed NGFW signs reissued certs with `Corp-Inspect-CA`. They said passthrough is configurable but might require policy exceptions per FQDN rather than just IP.

Anna - Support: Action plan:
- ECorp: configure the NGFW to set TLS passthrough for `private-controlplane.us-west-2.redwood.example` (or create an exception by FQDN). If passthrough is not possible, the NGFW must forward the original client cert via TLS proxying which is rare.
- ECorp: while changing, try a temporary test from a host that egresses through a different path (dev VPC works) to validate control plane accepts raw mTLS.
- Redwood: we'll pull control plane logs for the fingerprint you DM'ed and check for client cert presence/validation errors.

Jia - Eng-Infra: I pulled control plane logs for that window. Entry: `auth: mTLS client cert missing; connection reset after ClientHello; src egress 52.9.33.120`. No client cert presented to our backend. That matches NGFW termination.

ecrop-netops: Ok we'll try to set passthrough. One additional question: could MTU/TCP window clamp cause fragmentation that the NGFW mishandles and then resets? We did recently change MTU on the egress device.

Michael - EngOncall: It's possible but less likely: fragmentation typically causes retransmits, not CA errors. However, some NGFWs mis-handle TLS ClientHello fragmentation badly. If you see ClientHello split across multiple TCP segments in your capture, try increasing MTU or disabling TCP MSS clamping temporarily.

ecrop-netops: I checked tcpdump: ClientHello appears in a single packet ~1.3KB. Not fragmented.

Lena - Security: Also confirm ALPN: some proxies strip `h2`/`http/1.1` and servers with strict ALPN checks might abort. But again, our logs show missing client cert more than ALPN.

Anna - Support: Can we get a short repro checklist for documentation? I'll log this as an escalation so the customer success team can follow-up.

Michael - EngOncall: Repro checklist:
1) From a host behind the problematic egress path, run: `openssl s_client -connect private-controlplane.us-west-2.redwood.example:443 -tls1_2 -tls1_3 -cert client.pem -key client.key -showcerts -msg -alpn h2,http/1.1` and confirm ServerHello + Verify succeed.
2) tcpdump capture with `tcp port 443` and check for `ServerHello` packet or RST from proxy.
3) If RST from proxy, update NGFW to TLS passthrough for the FQDN or bypass deep inspection for control plane IPs.
4) If passthrough not possible, escalate to NGFW vendor for how to preserve client cert to origin (rare).

ecrop-netops: We'll implement passthrough exception and report back in ~30 min. Thanks.

(30 minutes later)

ecrop-netops: Update: configured passthrough by FQDN on the NGFW. Re-tested with `curl` using client cert -> succeeded. `openssl s_client` now shows ServerHello and Verified OK. No more RSTs.

Anna - Support: Great news! We'll keep monitoring. @Jia I flagged the original alert as user-caused (proxy rewrite) but left follow-up tasks to improve our KB on Private control plane network requirements (SNI passthrough, TLS passthrough, ALPN, MTU notes).

Jia - Eng-Infra: I'll open an internal doc and add the note: "For Private control plane, outbound egress proxies must allow TLS passthrough for mutual TLS endpoints (do not terminate and reissue certs). Ensure SNI and ALPN preserved; avoid ClientHello fragmentation."

Lena - Security: I'll add a short blurb on why TLS termination breaks mTLS — for security teams that assume inspection is always ok.

Michael - EngOncall: Closing this thread. If any new failures occur after changes, please re-open with tcpdump and openssl snippets. :thumbsup:

ecrop-netops: Thanks everyone :pray:
